Thanks again for the time today — great first call. Quick recap of what we heard, the key constraints, and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. Please flag anything I misrepresented.

Summary of pain / goals (from PixelGrid):
- Latency: user-facing completions should feel snappy — target p95 <= 150 ms for short interactive prompts (<= 256 tokens).
- Throughput: initial pilot ~300 concurrent sessions (expected 6–8 RPS sustained across peak windows), plan to scale to 2k concurrent within 6 months.
- Model quality: foundation-level generation with domain-tuning (financial docs) — want open-model family (Mistral / Llama variants) or Redwood-verified equivalents.
- Data residency: US-only, must integrate with their VPC and comply with retention policy (30 days, logs to SIEM).

Technical constraints called out on the call:
- Average prompt length low, but context windows up to 4k tokens for some workflows.
- Hard SLA: 99.5% availability during business hours; graceful degradation acceptable (fallback model) when capacity constrained.
- Security: SOC2 + customer-managed KMS preferred.

Redwood inference fit (high level):
- Serving pattern: recommend Dedicated pool for pilot (predictable throughput) + Hosted fallback for spikes.
- Optimizations to meet p95 <=150ms: model quantization (4-bit), KV cache for repeated prefixes, and short-sequence kernel selection.
- Topology sketch: primary nodes in us-east-1 (G5-style GPUs), separate async workers for long-context jobs, autoscale policy with warm standby.

Attachments included: pixelgrid_inference_requirements_20270502.xlsx (I exported the notes/metrics you shared) and our one-pager on Dedicated.

Next steps / owners:
1) Marcus to draft a lightweight topology diagram + sizing for the pilot (G5 vs A10 alternatives) — ETA Tue 5/4. (Owner: Marcus)
2) PixelGrid to share representative prompt set and 24h traffic sample (anonymized) — ETA Tue 5/4. (Owner: Rajiv)
3) Schedule a deep-dive with infra/ops to validate VPC & KMS requirements — propose Wed 5/5 11am ET. (Owner: Vanessa)
4) I’ll send a short mutual action plan and follow-up calendar invites after Marcus’s sizing.

If that looks right, Rajiv — can you confirm the sample traffic and your availability for Wed?

Thanks,

Thanks Rajiv — I’ll include fallback latency numbers and a concrete pilot sizing. Quick technical notes that I’m including here so PixelGrid has something to review before the Wed infra call: 

Pilot sizing assumptions (proposed):
- Target sustained RPS at pilot: 8 RPS (300 concurrent sessions x 0.025 RPS/session average) with 20% burst headroom -> target 10 RPS sustained for sizing.
- Recommended primary: 4x GPUs (A10G/G5 equivalent) in a dedicated pool for low-latency sync endpoints; NVMe-backed local cache for KV/prefix caching.
- Fallback (cost-savings): single-node pool of 7B quantized models (4-bit) for degraded mode — expected p95 ~220-300ms for short prompts (empirical).

Latency tuning levers:
- Kernel selection: shorter seq kernels for <=256 tokens; use fused-attention where supported.
- Continuous batching: keep batch sizes low for interactive but allow opportunistic batching during micro-peaks.
- Prefix & KV cache: serve repeated patterns from cache to cut token compute by ~30% on average.

Topology sketch (text):
- VPC-connected Dedicated inference cluster (us-east-1) with two AZs, warm standby in a second region for DR.
- Control plane (hosted) manages model routing; requests route to Dedicated pool when available, fallback to hosted pool (quantized smaller model) during autoscale cooldowns.
- Audit logs forwarded to your SIEM via S3 + KMS envelope encryption.

I’ll attach the sizing spreadsheet and a short table with expected p50/p95 numbers across model variants. Marcus
